message.content:
{
  "trigger": "Paper proposes a novel algorithm or metric and claims domain-specific advantages (e.g., handling temporal/ordered data) but evaluates primarily on standard, general-purpose benchmarks where it underperforms established baselines.",
  "review_heuristic": "Verify that the claimed domain-specific benefits are supported by experiments on relevant domain-specific datasets. If the method underperforms strong general baselines on standard benchmarks, assess whether the paper clearly defines the specific niche where it is superior or if the lack of performance indicates a fundamental flaw in the generalization capability.",
  "evidence_to_check": "Comparison tables against state-of-the-art baselines on both standard and domain-specific datasets; discussion of computational complexity and practical feasibility; theoretical justification for why the new method should outperform existing ones in specific scenarios.",
  "failure_mode": "The paper makes broad claims about domain impact (e.g., temporal data) without providing empirical evidence on that specific domain, while simultaneously failing to demonstrate competitive performance on standard benchmarks, leading to a lack of demonstrated significance or practical utility.",
  "why_it_matters": "Significance is determined by both the importance of the problem and the magnitude of the improvement. A method that is theoretically interesting but practically inferior to existing tools, or that fails to validate its specific niche claims, does not advance the state of the art or provide value to the community.",
  "reviewer_dimension": "SIGN"
}
